messages:
infra-bot: alert: prod-g5x p99 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~720ms around 15:09 UTC :rotating_light:
maria: saw the alert, correlates with driver rollout at 15:07 (nvidia 520.61 -> 525.10, CUDA 12.3 -> 13.0)
ajay: grafana shows spike aligning with rollout window, opening thread to collect traces
kevin: flamegraph (trace id trace-prod-20641) points to lots of time in kernel_selector::score_candidates and repeated KV cache eviction events
sara: ran a quick canary repro with mixed short/long seq (65% 8, 35% 512) on a g5x VM, observed selector switching from flash to gemm mid-run and workspace jumps
ajay: if selector flips to GEMM for short batches we increase per-batch workspace, which can push us over KV cache memory thresholds and cause eviction thrash
maria: profiler snippet pasted:```
2026-03-17T15:10:12Z selector: evaluated candidates [flash,gemm], scores [0.48,0.75], chose GEMM
2026-03-17T15:10:12Z launch GEMM workspace=1.9GB -> fallback path triggered -> KV_EVICT start
2026-03-17T15:10:12Z kv_hit_rate -9% -> p99 latency +450ms
```
kevin: telemetry shows KV hit rate for that pool dropped ~10% during spike, consistent with profiler
sara: digging deeper: CUDA 13.0 release notes mention occupancy changes; I think cuOccupancy heuristics changed which shifts Triton/autoselect occupancy estimates. That would explain gemm being favored more often
ajay: mitigation idea: add a short-seq bias to prefer flash attention for mean_seq < 128 while we investigate. Might slightly affect p50 on long seqs but reduce p99 tail risk
maria: pushed runtime flag --prefer-kernel=flash_short to canary at 15:39 UTC (via runtime-config), monitoring now
ops: rolled config to 50% of g5x capacity at 15:46, no downstream failures observed
kevin: after flag applied p99 dropped from ~720ms -> ~270ms within ~6 minutes, KV hit rate recovered
sara: repro commands and reproducer harness saved to runbooks: /runbooks/perf/kernel-occupancy-repro (also uploaded traces)
kevin: repro command used:```
python tools/repro_cli.py --target prod-g5x --pattern mixed --seq-dist "short:0.65:8,long:0.35:512" --duration 5m --collect-traces
```
maria: root cause summary to capture: CUDA 13 occupancy change -> Triton/autoselect chooses GEMM more frequently for certain mixed batch shapes -> GEMM uses larger workspace -> KV eviction thrash -> p99 spike
ajay: follow-ups: (1) add regression unit test for bimodal seq distributions to ensure selector stability, (2) file issue with Triton regarding occupancy behavior on CUDA13, (3) add adaptive workspace penalty when KV pressure metrics high so selector avoids workspace-heavy kernels under cache pressure
kevin: I'll add telemetry metric `kernel_selector_flip_rate` and a dashboard to catch this earlier
sara: also queue running Triton CI matrix against CUDA 13 to surface changes earlier, assigning to eng-ml oncall next week
maria: created follow-up ticket ENG-5241 and assigned to eng-runtime + eng-ml, uploaded flamegraphs and snapshots to s3://redwood-prod/perf/2064123457-occupancy-investigation
ops: incident mitigated after 30m stable with config flag in place, no rollback required :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks for quick response everyone. tagging @kevin @sara @ajay for postmortem writeup, will draft in #postmortems later today :heart:
ops: :thumbsup:
